geometry_edits.rationale: Increase the cantilever projection to make the dominant mass and its ground response more legible from the access edge.
Orient the courtyard opening to the verified access side to strengthen the public threshold.
Expand the void so it reads as a usable court and not just a minor notch.

graph_edits.rationale: Shift the cantilever toward a clearer access-side threshold without erasing the dominant bent-bar gesture.
Align the public void with the verified access side so the court reads as a legible neighborhood threshold.
Open the courtyard more so it functions as usable public space rather than a decorative subtraction.

rationale: The candidate reads as one coherent massing idea in all four views: a compact bent bar with a top-heavy/cantilevered upper volume and a carved relief near one side. It is not perfect, but it is legible and not colliding across views. The parcel response is acceptable: the mass sits within the green boundary and does not ignore orientation, though the open-space logic is modest rather than strong. The biggest weakness is the street edge: the blue frontage is answered more by a sealed/oblique mass than by a clearly public court, seam, or undercut on the access side, so the neighborhood-living brief is only partially expressed. Programmatically it can plausibly support mixed neighborhood living/commercial use because the mass suggests an active lower volume with an upper hierarchy, but it needs a more explicit public threshold and cleaner access-side void to fully align with the semantic invariants.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Reference is taller and more tower-like than the candidate; transfer the massing logic, not the vertical proportion.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Stepped-but-coherent massing with a clear dominant volume and a cut/relief that keeps the composition legible across views.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Office typology and atrium proportion are not directly transferable as a finished form; use only the void-placement principle.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: A rectilinear main body with a central void/atrium can support a public threshold while preserving strong hierarchy.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Restaurant image is more explicitly single-story and canopy-driven; the candidate should not over-flatten into a kiosk-like object.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Low horizontal base with an articulated entry edge and attached vertical accent can create neighborhood-scale presence without sealing the ground.

warnings: The frontage response is weak relative to the verified access edge; the mass should open more legibly toward that side.
Void publicness is present but underdeveloped; it reads more as a subtraction than as usable public space.
The stepped/cantilevered upper form is coherent, but it should not become more fragmented in revision.
